title: bb_health embedding coverage: the per-symbol EXISTS must probe entity_id, and must still be project-scoped

checks.name: the executable code still contains per-symbol embedding EXISTS probes (the queries under test exist)
checks.detail: found 2 in code: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM brain_semantic_embedding e WHERE e.entit | EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM brain_semantic_embedding e WHERE e.entit

checks.name: NOT ONE of them re-filters project_id inside the EXISTS
checks.detail: 0 clause(s) still carry e.project_id:  — that predicate is what makes SQLite scan every embedding of the project once per symbol (~2,770s at 304,926 symbols)

checks.name: and the comment does not claim the index probe again [negative]
checks.detail: that claim was measured FALSE on a real index: the plan uses brain_embed_health_idx (project_id=?) and filters entity_id

checks.name: nor does it claim the scan is avoided [negative]
checks.detail: a comment asserting an unmeasured performance property is how this defect shipped with a gate suite green

checks.name: and the real-index measurement is recorded next to the fix
checks.detail: a fix whose magnitude is unrecorded will be re-litigated as 'probably fine' by the next reader — the measurement is the argument

checks.name: the fixture indexed symbols to work with
the fixture's own embeddings are cleared, so only planted rows can match
checks.detail: 0 embeddings left for this project — a test that cannot see its own fixture is a test that measures the fixture

checks.name: byLanguage is populated (the query ran, it did not fall into the catch)
checks.detail: 1 languages — 0 would mean the try/catch swallowed a failure, which reads as 'no coverage data' rather than as an error

checks.name: another project's embeddings are NOT counted as ours
checks.detail: embedded=0 against 3 symbols — a foreign entity_id must not match, and with the project_id predicate gone the entity_id IS the scope

checks.name: OUR OWN embedding IS counted — the fix did not over-correct
the cost fixture has enough symbols for a per-symbol scan to hurt
the plan probes the embedding table by ENTITY_ID, not by project_id
checks.detail: plan: SCAN s | CORRELATED SCALAR SUBQUERY 1 | SEARCH e USING COVERING INDEX brain_embed_entity_idx (entity_id=?)

checks.name: the plan assertion above is the load-bearing one, and it passed on entity_id
checks.detail: plan: SCAN s | CORRELATED SCALAR SUBQUERY 1 | SEARCH e USING COVERING INDEX brain_embed_entity_idx (entity_id=?) — the ratio is scale-dependent and is recorded, not asserted

checks.name: the report is still correct at that scale
checks.detail: byLanguage symbols total=8000 vs 8000 indexed — a fast query that returns the wrong number is worse than a slow one

decisions.why: a default call took >15 minutes on a real 6,507-file index because the per-symbol EXISTS re-filtered project_id and so scanned every embedding once per symbol
decisions.fix: drop the redundant project_id predicate; entity_id is minted as `${projectId}:...` for both brain_symbol.id and brain_semantic_embedding.entity_id, so the predicate cannot change the answer
decisions.gate: shape, scope and plan — never a clock, because a timing assertion is decided by contention and a fixture big enough to expose this honestly would be too slow to run every time

limitations: The real-index numbers (10.2ms/symbol, ~2,770s extrapolated, 513x speedup) came from the 1.6GB index at ~/.bb/projects/818db37d.../ and are NOT reproduced by this gate, which runs on a small fixture. The gate pins the query shape and the plan; the magnitude lives in reviews/health/master-review.md and is not re-measured on every run.

The equivalence of dropping project_id depends on the id convention `${projectId}:${rest}`. This gate pins that convention by planting a foreign-project embedding and requiring it to be ignored; it cannot prove the convention holds for code that does not exist yet.
